topic.title: Your Samosa Didn't Get Expensive On Its Own
topic.claim: Food prices creep up one rupee at a time so you never notice the real hike happening upstream.
topic.behaviour: Oil companies raised commercial LPG cylinder prices sharply while keeping the politically sensitive domestic cylinder price flat for the fifth straight month.
topic.mechanism: Protecting the visible domestic price looks good in a headline, letting the invisible commercial price absorb the hit, which then reaches you slowly, through the shopkeeper's plate, not a news story.
topic.group: anyone who's noticed their regular food order got quietly pricier
topic.moment: Your regular chai-samosa stall bumps the price by a few rupees, and you don't think twice about it.

turn.believed: Small vendors raise prices because costs rise everywhere, equally, all the time.
turn.actually: Commercial LPG, what every dhaba and food stall runs on, just got a steep hike, while the domestic cylinder stayed untouched.

topic.because: The domestic cylinder price is the one everyone notices, so it stays flat for optics, while the commercial cylinder quietly absorbs the real cost and small vendors pass it on, plate by plate.

proof.fact: Commercial 19kg LPG cylinder prices rose ₹62.50 to ₹71.50 across cities from October 1, while the domestic 14.2kg cylinder stayed unchanged for a fifth straight month

topic.payoff: When a price climbs a few rupees at a time, somewhere upstream, a bigger number just moved.
topic.send_to: anyone who's noticed their usual food order got pricier for no obvious reason
real_details: Patna saw the steepest commercial LPG hike, up ₹71.50 to ₹3,100.50
A ₹5 Lays packet marketed as 11g+1.3g actually weighed 4.32g on a gold scale
Tea alone now costs ₹20-30 in some places
Hyderabad street corners still serve a hot, filling breakfast for ₹25
topic.why_now: Shows up in food prices exactly as festive spending peaks

score.why: The chai-samosa price creep is something everyone's noticed and shrugged off; connecting it to the domestic-cylinder-stays-flat-for-optics trick gives it a because nobody had.

sources.fact: Oil marketing companies raised 19 kg commercial LPG prices by Rs 62.50–71.50 per cylinder from Oct 1, 2026, while the 14.2 kg domestic cylinder price stayed unchanged for the fifth consecutive month.
sources.excerpt: 19 Kg commercial LPG rates in the range of Rs 62.50 to Rs 71.50 per cylinder across major cities. | the domestic LPG cylinders or 14.2 Kg LPG prices remain unchanged for the fifth consecutive month. | The domestic LPG prices are kept the same since June 7, 2026.

sources.fact: The Delhi 19-kg commercial cylinder rose Rs 62.50 to Rs 2,810, Patna rose Rs 71.50 to Rs 3,100.50, and the household 14.2-kg cylinder stayed at Rs 942 in Delhi.
sources.excerpt: the price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder has increased by Rs 62.50, taking the latest rate to Rs 2,810 from Rs 2,747.50 in September | 19-kg cylinder prices rising by up to Rs 71.50 across cities | For households, however, there is no change in the price of the 14.2-kg domestic LPG cylinder.

cover.headline: Your samosa's two-rupee hike started [nowhere near the stall]
cover.sub: A price rise you paid without ever reading about it.

paragraphs: Your samosa's two-rupee hike started nowhere near the stall.
It's evening, the laptop is shut, and you're at the stall near the office. Two chai, one samosa, the paper plate going soft under the green chutney.
The change comes back a few rupees short. "Bhaiya, rate badh gaya?" He nods without looking up from the kadhai. You shrug and pick up the samosa.
slides.why_swipe: But was it really just everything getting costlier?

paragraphs: But one cost behind that counter jumped this month. The tall commercial gas cylinder every stall and dhaba cooks on went up by ₹62.50 to ₹71.50, depending on the city.
**The cylinder in your own kitchen didn't move at all.**
slides.why_swipe: Why would one cylinder jump and the other stay put?

paragraphs: The home cylinder is the price you notice. Every family checks it, the TV debates it, and a hike there becomes news within hours.
The commercial one has no audience. Nobody tweets about a dhaba's gas bill.
**So its hike reaches you only through a plate, with no headline attached.**
slides.why_swipe: So is bhaiya the one squeezing you?

paragraphs: And bhaiya isn't going to stick a notice on the stall about his gas bill. His regulars would just walk to the next one.
So he spreads one bigger bill across a month of plates, a rupee here, two there. Fair enough. He's not the one who raised it.
slides.why_swipe: So what do you do with this the next time it happens?

paragraphs: Next time your usual order creeps up, look behind the counter before you blame the stall.
If there's a gas cylinder standing there, you already paid this month's hike. You just paid it in samosas.

end.save: Come back to it the next time your usual order costs a few rupees more.
end.send: Send it to the friend who still splits the chai bill to the rupee.

draft.caption: What's the one thing at your regular stall that's gone up a few rupees this year without anyone saying a word?
draft.alt_text: A six-slide carousel. The cover says your samosa's two-rupee hike started nowhere near the stall. The slides follow a reader at their regular evening chai and samosa stall, getting back a few rupees less change and shrugging it off. It then points out that this month the commercial gas cylinder stalls and dhabas cook on went up by ₹62.50 to ₹71.50 depending on the city, while the home cylinder price did not change. It argues the home price is the one everyone watches, so the commercial hike reaches people only through plate prices, and the vendor spreads it out a rupee at a time. It ends by saying that if there's a gas cylinder behind the counter, you already paid this month's hike, just in samosas.

claims.text: This month the commercial gas cylinder every stall and dhaba cooks on went up by ₹62.50 to ₹71.50, depending on the city.
The domestic (home) LPG cylinder price did not change.
